Orlando

Best Family Activities In Orlando

By Marcus Webb · April 8, 2026 · Updated August 24, 2026 · 8 min read

Orlando trips tend to get planned entirely around which parks to visit on which days, and it’s easy to forget the city has a lot to offer outside the resorts. The activities in this guide are the ones worth trading a park day for — either as a rest day or because they’re genuinely good on their own terms.

Quick facts

Best for a rest day
Lake Eola Park or a springs day trip
Getting around
Rental car recommended — Orlando is spread out

Orlando is more than its theme parks

A week in Orlando built entirely around theme parks can wear a family out faster than it needs to. Some of the best days on an Orlando trip are the ones that step outside the parks entirely — cheaper, less crowded, and a genuine change of pace.

Beyond the big parks

Gatorland

A smaller, old-school attraction that consistently overdelivers relative to its size — alligator shows, a zipline, and a fraction of the crowds of the major parks.

Kennedy Space Center

About an hour east of Orlando, and worth the drive — genuinely engaging for kids who claim not to like museums, with real rockets and, occasionally, a scheduled launch visible from the grounds.

Natural springs (Wekiwa or Blue Spring)

Constant 72°F spring-fed water, far less crowded than a resort pool, and a good antidote to a few days of theme park heat and lines.

Lake Eola Park, Downtown Orlando

Swan-shaped paddle boats and a walkable loop around the lake — a low-key, low-cost afternoon that works well as a rest day.

Making a multi-day Orlando trip work

  • Plan a non-park day for roughly every three park days — it noticeably improves everyone's mood for the days that follow
  • Book character dining experiences well ahead if that's a priority; the popular ones book out weeks in advance
  • Afternoon thunderstorms are a near-daily summer occurrence — plan indoor or pool time for early-to-mid afternoon in June through September
  • Consider a mid-trip laundry stop rather than overpacking; most Orlando-area rentals and many hotels have machines

Where to stay for easy access

  • Resorts directly on Disney or Universal property offer the most convenience but at a price premium
  • The International Drive corridor offers a wide range of hotel prices with reasonable proximity to most major parks
  • Kissimmee-area vacation home rentals are often the best value for larger families, usually with a private pool

Frequently asked questions

How many days should you spend in Orlando outside the theme parks?

For a week-long trip, we'd suggest one to two non-park days — enough to rest without losing the momentum of a theme-park-focused trip.

Is Kennedy Space Center worth the drive from Orlando?

Yes, for most families — it's about an hour east and offers a genuinely different experience from the parks, with strong appeal even for kids who aren't typically drawn to museums.

What's a good rest-day activity in Orlando?

A natural spring like Blue Spring or Wekiwa, or a low-key afternoon at Lake Eola Park downtown — both offer a real change of pace from theme park crowds and heat.
